selected_evidence.requirement: node2 HTTP service on 8080 exists and is healthy (baseline)
selected_evidence.summary: Installed python3 and started 'python3 -m http.server 8080' on node2, confirmed the process persists across exec calls and serves 'hello-from-node2' locally

selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline: node3 could reach node2 directly on 8080, but node1:80 was not yet publishing the service
selected_evidence.summary: wget from node3 to 10.100.226.11:8080 succeeded (direct-exit=0); wget to 10.100.226.10:80 failed (via-node1-exit=5) before configuration

selected_evidence.requirement: Publish node2:8080 on node1's outward-facing address port 80 (DNAT port-forward)
selected_evidence.summary: Added OPNsense NAT port-forward rule (lan:80 -> 10.100.226.11:8080) via config.xml edit, reloaded filter, and confirmed 'rdr pass on vtnet0 ... port = http -> 10.100.226.11 port 8080' present in pfctl -s nat

selected_evidence.requirement: Root-caused and fixed anti-lockout rule blocking the port-forward on port 80
selected_evidence.summary: pfctl showed 'no rdr on vtnet0 ... port = http' exemption; disabled system/webgui/noantilockout and confirmed the exemption was removed from pfctl -s nat

selected_evidence.requirement: node3 reaches the service through node1's address, not node2 directly (hairpin NAT working, evidence node3 is not just falling back to direct access)
selected_evidence.summary: Initial attempts hung; tcpdump on node1 vtnet0 showed only node1<->node3 traffic (proxy-like, wrong response), and pfctl -s states showed CLOSED:SYN_SENT to node2, proving asymmetric routing / no reply reaching node1

selected_evidence.requirement: Fix asymmetric routing with hairpin SNAT and confirm working hairpin NAT
selected_evidence.summary: Added hybrid-mode outbound NAT rule rewriting LAN traffic destined to node2:8080 to node1's LAN IP; wget from node3 to 10.100.226.10:80 now returns 'hello-from-node2', and node2's access log shows the request sourced from 10.100.226.10 (node1), not 10.100.226.12 (node3)

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, boot identity change, recovery
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime captured; issued 'shutdown -r now'; exec unreachable during reboot; kern.boottime changed from 16:32:46 to 16:43:32 after recovery; pfctl -s nat rules persisted and node3->node1:80 request succeeded post-restart

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, boot identity change, recovery
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 6ce4ebc2...; issued 'reboot'; new boot_id 7747d020... confirms restart; index.html data persisted, HTTP service process (not a persistent unit) was restarted, and end-to-end hairpin request from node3 succeeded post-restart

selected_evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, boot identity change, recovery
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id b954f5de...; issued 'reboot'; new boot_id d4bee8af... confirms restart; post-restart wget from node3 to node1:80 succeeded, and node2's access log shows the request sourced from node1's IP, confirming full recovery of the hairpin NAT path
